body:
Tested locally, it works as expected.

Some issues I noticed:

- On KDE X11, if I hold <kbd>Windows</kbd> and use the left and right mouse button, I can move/resize windows without needing to drag their border. This is usually fine, but it lets me resize the inner game window within a floating game window, which I'm not supposed to be able to do:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57c94845-9bb7-47be-81a7-f95b609654ad

- These menu options should be renamed to hint that they only take effect starting from the next play session (if you use them while the project is running):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d133e49b-87c6-4868-9385-87110cbb9e78)

I suggest **Embed Game on Next Play** and **Make Game Workspace Floating on Next Play**.

Tested on Windows 11 and Linux (both X11 and X Wayland) it seems to work as expected.

Embedded window lags when resizing/moving parent window (a bit on Windows, and a lot on X11).

The only issue I see, there seems to be no way to control default behavior, it is saved on a per-project basis, but for new projects it defaults to "Make Game Workspace floating" (the least useful mode in my opinion).

I get this when switching to the "Game" tab:
```
E 0:00:00:0127   window_set_position: Embedded window can't be moved.
  <C++ Error>    Condition "wd.embed_parent" is true.
  <C++ Source>   platform/linuxbsd/x11/display_server_x11.cpp:2265 @ window_set_position()
```
Fedora GNU/Linux 41 (XWayland).
No errors on my end now, good job! I think there are still some stuff that could use some polish, but nothing deal breaking. LGTM.
